## Design note

The modern patrol utility: AWD launches and a twin-turbo punch make it the quickest of the tall police units, and the unibody keeps it far more agile than the Bastion. Push bar up front for shoving; it rolls less than the old SUV but still leans hard and runs out of grip before the sedans do.

## How this car breaks

Modern UHSS unibody with the police push bar bolted through to the front rails and a doubled bumper beam: shunts bend the bar first. No ladder frame, so a hit hard enough to get past the bar crushes the rails like a car's. The cargo bay behind the rear seat is not passenger cell; the high CG trips it in hard side hits at the wheels.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| roll | 1308 | 0.82 | 1070 |
| pitch | 5230 | 0.93 | 4860 |

3.5 L DOHC V6, twin turbo, direct injection, police calibration. Class-typical late-2010s 3.5 TT V6 (~80 kW/L, ~281 kW at 5500 rpm, ~515 N·m from 2500) per fleet spec-class data — the Wolfhound's engine family in its later utility tune.

## Drivetrain

6-speed automatic with torque converter, on-demand AWD (90 % front until the fronts slip 2 %, then up to 50 % rear), open diffs. Layout **on-demand AWD, 90 % front with the coupling open, up to 50 % rear once the fronts out-spin the rears by 2 %**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Torque converter: stall 2600 rpm, 1.9× at stall, couples 1:1 from 3000 rpm (class-typical for the gearbox). Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 820 N·m. Shift time 0.30 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |

| 1 | 4.48 | 15.19 | 55 |
| 2 | 2.87 | 9.73 | 85 |
| 3 | 1.84 | 6.24 | 133 |
| 4 | 1.41 | 4.78 | 173 |

Final drive 3.39, reverse 2.88. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.366 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 581 kg | 1.40 Hz | 44900 N/m | 3070 N·s/m | 4600 N·s/m | 0.19 m |
| Rear | 450 kg | 1.50 Hz | 39900 N/m | 2540 N·s/m | 3810 N·s/m | 0.20 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 3.6°/g with 62% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.562 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 192205 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 64951 F / 57703 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **18800 F / 5300 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 3.6°/g, front share 62%. Bump stops 220000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -0.5° F / -0.7° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.15° R (+ = in), caster 5.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 363 mm disc, pistons per side 54 mm + 54 mm → A = 45.8 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 156 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·45.8 cm²·0.157 m = **6021 N·m**
- Rear: 345 mm disc, pistons per side 44 mm → A = 15.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 148 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·15.2 cm²·0.147 m = **1794 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 6021 / 1794 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.14), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.87 → **5230 / 1560 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 3061 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.71×), rear needs 872 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.79×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 1491 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.511** → delivered 5230 N·m front / 1493 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1260 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 16.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 12.0 m → outer-front path radius 5.87 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.18 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.626 rad (35.9°)** (outer 31.0°, inner 42.2° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.60). Rack speed 1.3 rad/s.

304 nodes, 1988 beams, 9 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Steel hood: 132 hood beams aluminum → mild_steel.
- Detachables: steel bumpers ×2.3 break impulse / ×4 mass; steel hood ×1.4 / ×1.6.
- Luggage bay: 13 Cabin nodes behind the rear seatback (y < -1.61 m, rear axle −0.10 m) relabelled FrameRear — the passenger cell ends at the seatback, as on a real two-box body.
- Push bar: 4 extra Accessory-region nodes 0.10 m ahead of the bumper (z 0.45/0.95 m), hss 1.2e-03 m² tubes bolted to the bumper-beam rail nodes with 9.0e-04 m² mounts; detachable group 8, 30000 N·s, 40 kg. Front bumper beam ×2 (2 beams), as gen-lattice's cruiser profile does.
- Police package: heavy-duty components fail at × the stock intrusion (Battery ×1.3, BrakeFL ×1.3, BrakeFR ×1.3, Engine ×1.2, Radiator ×1.5, SteeringRack ×1.5, SuspensionFL ×1.5, SuspensionFR ×1.5, WheelFL ×1.4, WheelFR ×1.4); front bumper fixings ×2.0 detach impulse.
